entries.content: Use table-driven tests with named cases for Go packages.
Keep final answers concise and lead with the result.
Schedule reminders using Europe/Lisbon local time.
Avoid peanuts because of an allergy.
Before merging Atlas changes, run go test ./... and go vet ./....
The host opens and closes the SQLite database. Stores borrow the database handle.
An interrupted Atlas execution resumes only after an explicit user action. Queued requests wait.
Cancelling the active Atlas execution advances the queue to the next request.
The current command to deploy the Atlas service to staging is make deploy ENV=staging. This does not publish a production release.
Apply Atlas database migrations using make migrate before deployment.
Read AGENTS.md in the workspace before editing Atlas source files.
Configure query and document prefixes separately. The embedding model may need a task instruction before a query while documents are embedded without that instruction.
Atlas memory uses BM25 keyword ranking. Search with distinctive names and identifiers.
Canonical memory entries are authoritative. Indexes hold derived representations.
Rebuild the memory index from canonical entries after an indexing failure.
Before merging Beacon changes, run npm test and npm run lint.
The Beacon store owns its SQLite database and closes it when disposed.
Beacon resumes interrupted jobs automatically on startup.
Deploy the Beacon service using npm run deploy -- --production.
Deploy the Atlas service using make child-deploy ENV=production.
When explaining an architecture, include a small diagram showing the main components and how requests move between them.
During a long task, report progress after finishing a meaningful step. Include what was learned and what will happen next.
Format source code snippets in fenced code blocks with the language name. Keep shell commands separate from application source.
Give Go tests descriptive names that explain the behavior being checked. Avoid abbreviations such as TestMisc and TestStuff.
Keep integration checks separate from quick unit tests. Integration checks should use real temporary SQLite databases and temporary files, without depending on an external production service.
Use property-based testing for parsers with many combinations of input. Keep a small set of regression examples for previously reported parsing failures.
Prefer vegetarian lunches on weekdays. This is a meal preference and does not identify an allergy.
Avoid coffee and other caffeine after 15:00 because it disrupts sleep.
Do not schedule reminder notifications between 22:00 and 07:00 local time. Deliver a reminder in the morning if its requested time falls inside this quiet interval.
Use 25 minutes as the default meeting duration when no duration was requested.
Leave a twenty-minute travel buffer between meetings that take place in different physical locations.
Use tabs for indentation in Go source files and two spaces per indentation level in YAML configuration files.
Wrap prose at about one hundred columns when editing Markdown files. Do not reflow generated files or source snippets just to satisfy that preference.
Ask before recursively deleting a working directory or an entire repository. Deleting a single temporary file created during the current task does not need a separate approval.
Write replies in English unless the current conversation explicitly requests another language.
When explaining a formula, define each term before deriving the result and show a small numerical example.
Send a desktop notification after a background job finishes or requires attention. Do not send a notification for every individual tool call.
Review correctness and data-loss risks before style issues. In a code review, lead with the most consequential finding.
Use Celsius for temperatures and kilometers for distances in personal planning.
Use British spelling in prose written for me, while preserving identifiers and quoted source text.
Never put API keys, passwords, or recovery codes in durable memory entries. Refer to the credential location rather than copying the secret.

The default Atlas settings file is ~/.config/atlas/settings.yaml. It contains model selection, tool settings, and storage locations. The --config argument chooses another settings file; it does not change the working directory of an existing session. Logs live under the cache directory, not beside this configuration file.
ATLAS_CONFIG overrides the Atlas settings file location. ATLAS_HOME changes the cache root. Setting ATLAS_HOME does not select a different settings file.
Atlas stores session transcript files under ~/.local/share/atlas/sessions/<session-id>.jsonl. These JSONL files contain conversation and execution history; they are not the durable knowledge store.
Each Atlas session persists its working directory under the session-state key workdir. Relative tool paths use this directory rather than the host process directory.
Set cmd.Dir to the current Atlas session working directory for each bash invocation. Running cd inside one subprocess does not change the directory used by later bash or filesystem tool calls.

Atlas file reads and writes resolve relative paths against the session working directory. Absolute paths are used as supplied. The filesystem tools do not follow the most recent directory change inside a bash subprocess.

Atlas captures environment instructions once at the beginning of each execution. A working-directory change during a running execution is reflected in the instructions of the next execution, not by rewriting the active request.
Queued Atlas executions run in first-in, first-out order. A session has at most one active execution. Persist the waiting requests before acknowledging their admission.
Cancelling a queued Atlas request removes that waiting request only. It does not interrupt the execution that is already running.
Use /resume <execution-id> to continue an interrupted Atlas execution. The resumed work keeps the same execution identity. /new starts a separate conversation instead.
On Ctrl+C, Atlas stops admitting work, cancels the active model or tool call, and flushes durable entries. Queued requests remain persisted and do not run during shutdown.
Conversation compaction keeps a summary of earlier work plus retained recent messages. A later compaction receives the previous summary so important decisions can survive progressive summarisation.
Automatic Atlas compaction starts when the estimated request context reaches eighty percent of the configured model context limit. Tool output truncation is a separate operation.
Use /compact to request conversation compaction explicitly. It reduces conversation history and does not delete entries from durable memory storage.

Atlas durable knowledge entries live in ~/.local/share/atlas/memories.json. Session transcripts stay in the sessions directory as JSONL. Moving a transcript does not move or delete the knowledge entries.
Atlas uses personal and project namespaces for durable memory. Scopes are exact strings: project:atlas does not automatically include project:atlas/child.

When a memory update returns ErrConflict, another writer has advanced the entry version. Read the latest entry, review its content, and apply the intended change with that current version. Do not retry with the stale version or overwrite the concurrent change blindly.
Deleting a canonical Atlas memory notifies each indexer to remove its representation. Retrieval loads canonical entries and excludes a deleted entry even if removal from an index fails.
Atlas does not automatically consolidate related memories in the background. Save or revise durable knowledge when explicitly requested, and keep temporary task progress in session history.

A saved vector represents one canonical entry ID, version, and embedding space. Reuse the vector only when both its entry version and its embedding space match the current entry and embedder; otherwise regenerate its embedding.

At startup the Atlas vector index removes orphaned vectors whose canonical entries no longer exist. It also populates missing or outdated representations before accepting searches. Keep canonical writes stopped during this initial reconciliation.

The Atlas local embedding model is qwen3-embedding:0.6b. Changing the configured model selects a different embedding space; a model tag alone does not identify a particular downloaded weight revision.
Send embedding requests to the Ollama /api/embed endpoint at localhost:11434. The /api/chat endpoint generates chat responses and is not the endpoint used by the Atlas embedder.

The Atlas vector store performs exact cosine similarity search within the requested embedding space and scope. Higher similarity scores rank first. It does not use an approximate nearest-neighbour graph or treat the score as a distance.

Atlas hybrid search combines BM25 and vector result rankings with reciprocal rank fusion. The default RRF rank constant is 60. Fusion uses positions in each ranking rather than directly adding unrelated keyword and cosine scores.

The Atlas search pipeline requests up to one hundred candidates from each retriever before applying the final result limit. It resolves canonical entries and discards missing, stale, or out-of-scope candidates before merging. Asking for three final memories can therefore search a much larger candidate pool.
An empty or whitespace-only search query returns no candidates from Atlas keyword and vector retrieval. Memory.Search retrieves saved entries; it does not ask a language model to invent an answer.
The Atlas host registers the modernc SQLite driver before opening a database. The core memory package does not import a database driver; storage/sqlite.New accepts an already opened *sql.DB.
For Atlas backups, use the database backup operation supplied by the host. Do not implement backups by copying only memory.db while its WAL file may contain committed changes.

Atlas database startup configures journal_mode(WAL), busy_timeout(5000), and foreign_keys(ON) on host-owned connections. These settings belong to database composition, not to the memory Store constructor.

The Atlas reporting connection opens an existing database with mode=ro. Reports may list saved entries but must not create memories, run migrations, or repair index state through that read-only connection.
ERR_SESSION_READ_ONLY means an Atlas session was opened in read-only mode. Reopen that session as writable before running tools that modify its working directory or submitting a mutating execution.

ERR_SESSION_INTERRUPTED identifies an Atlas execution that stopped before completion. It is distinct from an individual model request timeout. Continue the interrupted execution through explicit resume.
ERR_REQUEST_TIMEOUT means a single Atlas model request exceeded its ninety-second deadline. Retrying that request is different from restoring an interrupted execution after application shutdown.

Atlas limits inline tool output to 8 KiB and stores the full output as an attachment. The model receives a short preview and a reference for reading more. This output cap is separate from conversation compaction and model output-token limits.

Historical note from 2024: Atlas staging used scripts/push-staging.sh. That script was retired in 2025 and must not be used for current staging deployments. Keep the note only to explain old incident reports.

Atlas production releases require a version tag and make release TAG=<version>. The staging deploy command does not publish production. Release notes and a successful migration check are required before publishing the tag.
To roll back an Atlas application release, run make rollback RELEASE=<previous-tag>. This selects the earlier application image; it does not automatically reverse database schema changes.
Store Atlas provider credentials in the operating-system keychain. Settings contain provider IDs and model names, not plaintext API keys. Credentials are loaded by the host before model construction.
Beacon reads beacon.toml from its process working directory. BEACON_PROFILE chooses a named configuration profile rather than an Atlas settings file.
Beacon captures the process working directory at startup. Its sessions do not persist a per-session workdir field.
Beacon runs up to four jobs concurrently and chooses the highest-priority waiting job first. This worker-pool policy is separate from Atlas session scheduling.
Cancelling an active Beacon job pauses its queue until an operator acknowledges the cancellation. It does not advance the next request automatically.
On SIGTERM, Beacon waits for its currently running job to finish before shutting down. Waiting jobs remain in the external broker.
Beacon conversation compaction rewrites the complete older transcript into one summary and keeps the most recent user turn. The policy is not the Atlas retained-message policy.
Beacon uses a hosted embedding provider with separate document and query endpoints. It does not send embedding requests to localhost Ollama.
Beacon memory keyword retrieval uses trigram matching. BM25 is not the configured keyword algorithm for this project.
Beacon reconstructs its current memory view from an immutable event log. Its canonical storage model is independent of the Atlas current-entry store.
In Beacon, ERR_SESSION_READ_ONLY indicates that a request reached a read-only replica. Retry against the primary endpoint rather than reopening an Atlas session.
Beacon model requests have a thirty-second deadline and may retry once automatically. This is not the Atlas ninety-second request policy.
Historical Beacon deployments used node scripts/release.js. This retired command was replaced before the current production deployment process.
Beacon prepares release artifacts with npm run release. Artifact preparation alone does not deploy the service to production.
Roll back a Beacon service deployment with beaconctl rollback --service api. The project does not provide an Atlas make rollback target.
Beacon obtains its provider token from BEACON_TOKEN in the worker environment. It does not use the Atlas operating-system keychain integration.
Beacon reports cosine distance in its search diagnostics, where lower values indicate nearer records. Those diagnostics are not Atlas cosine similarity scores.
Atlas child jobs resolve relative paths against the child checkout directory, not the parent Atlas session working directory.
Before merging the Atlas child Rust service, run cargo test and cargo clippy. The parent project Go test commands do not apply to this scope.
The project:atlas/child scope stores child-service decisions only. Selecting project:atlas must not implicitly include these entries.
The Atlas child service settings live in .atlas-child/config.json inside the child checkout. They are not the parent ~/.config/atlas/settings.yaml file.
